claims.paraphrase: Page title.
Page tagline.
Section heading.
Diagram: the tool creates or connects five assets, one of them a Cloudflare account with a Worker, two databases, one bucket.
Caption: the tool holds none of the assets afterward.
The tool builds and connects five things.
A private repository holds the site code and everything written, as markdown.
A GitHub App publishes for writers so none needs a GitHub account.
Your Cloudflare account runs one Worker, two databases, one image bucket.
Optional domain, present only when connected.
A sign-in database you control.
The assets belong to the operator, not to cairn.
Repository holds all content as plain markdown; cloning it is enough to leave.
Section heading.
Framing that three things stand between you and setup, two of them money.
Workers Paid costs five dollars a month per account from first deploy; a second site adds nothing.
A domain costs about ten to fifteen dollars a year from a registrar; Cloudflare sells at cost and shows the price.
You create an API token yourself; the first run does not ask for one.
The domain step opens Cloudflare create-token page with permissions preselected and asks you to paste the token.
Connecting to Workers Builds asks for a second, wider token.
Cloudflare can show a permission row as an empty control instead of an error.
A token missing a permission is accepted and fails later at the step needing it.
Confirm every requested row is filled in before creating the token.
Total about six dollars a month: five for Workers Paid plus roughly one for domain renewal.
Whether the custom-domain certificate is included in the plan is unconfirmed.
The tool prints these figures before asking anything.
Section heading.
A second editor needs a connected domain and Email Sending; a workers.dev-only site has no sender.
Without both, the site works the same and only the owner can sign in.
Pointers to the domain and invite pages.
Section heading.
Setup needs no code, but a few tasks need a developer.
Rotating the GitHub App key is a terminal and wrangler task for a developer.
Engine updates are a developer task; pointer to the upgrade page.
Building beyond what cairn ships belongs to the extend track.
Describes which conditions the readiness page routes to a developer.
Everything else in the track you do alone.
Section heading.
A successor needs GitHub collaborator access, Cloudflare account access, and an editor row.
Entries are plain markdown files in git with no database only cairn reads; leaving means cloning.
